items.title: Gordon Lorraine — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee discusses the song 'Ruby My Dear' and its origin, but 'Ruby' is identified as a girl's name/title for the composition, not a person the interviewee has a personal relationship with.

ctx.x: Oh, “Epistrophy.” That one really tongue-tied me for a while. Yeah. “Well, You Needn’t.” What a statement. But “Ruby My Dear,” I was... He didn’t have a title at the time, and

he would be playing that for me at home. He said he doesn’t have a title...it’s a girl’s name or something. I kept saying to him, “Gee, I wish you would call it ‘Lorraine, My Dear,’” but I said, “I already have a song, ‘Sweet Lorraine,’ so forget it, you’re not going to get it.” But I kind of was hankering for that one. “Ruby, My Dear.” I love that one. And what about “Round Midnight”? Did you ever hear such a blues like that? And then they put words to it. Everybody embellished everything he did. He was a true…
